newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi sends home bodies of crashed plane crew.
newsitem.headline: Saudi sends home bodies of crashed plane crew.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has sent home the remains of most non-Saudi crew members who died in the world's worst mid-air collision over India, Saudi officials said on Sunday.

Moroccan stewardess Bushra Kilani was buried by her family in the Saudi city of Mecca, home to one of Islam's holiest shrines at dawn on Saturday, said the Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp officials speaking by telephone from Jeddah.

The bodies of 14 of the 23 crew members, including four anti-terrorism security men, and one Saudi passenger who died in Tuesday's accident between a Saudi jumbo jet and a Kazakh airliner, arrived in Jeddah on Friday from New Delhi.
The body of Moroccan stewardess, Rashida Bou Azaa and of her Tunisian colleague Afaf Dakhli were sent home on Sunday, added the officials.
The body of the fourth stewardess will be sent to Algiers on Monday while the airline is waiting for the family of Jordanian Usama Usama Zaghl to arrive in the kingdom to collect his body.
The Saudi airliner with 312 people on board and a KazAir Ilyushin IL-76 freighter carrying 37 collided seven minutes after the Saudi plane had taken off from New Delhi. There were no survivors.
